definitions.meaning: keeping a tally of points in a game

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is tallying points in a match; the other is marked with incised lines, as a surface can be.

parts.note: a star is famous; star as an adjective means celebrated
a tout solicits custom, so a solicitor here is one who touts

explanation.surface: A famous lawyer is about to begin the case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' wants to be a lawyer, but here it is someone who solicits, a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin a journey or activity is to set off on it.

parts.note: a batter dismissed in cricket is out
just means fair or right

explanation.surface: Someone sacked only because they lacked qualifications.
explanation.definitionFit: Unqualified in the sense of complete or absolute, as in an outright win.

indicators.note: in a down light, rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: note means distinction or repute, as in a person of note

explanation.surface: A fee-paying school whose standing is improving.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'public school' is a famous fee-paying independent school; this one is near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Founded by Henry VI, it is England's best-known fee-paying boarding school.

definitions.meaning: a sharp, sour-tongued remark is a cutting jibe
a boiled confection with a sharp sour flavour

explanation.definitionFit: A sour boiled confection sold in British sweetshops, and figuratively a person or remark with a sharp, sour edge.

parts.note: Tony Benn, the Labour politician, sat in Parliament for this Derbyshire town; the word is also a buttoned leather sofa

explanation.walkthrough: Tony Benn was a British Labour MP whose last constituency was this Derbyshire town; the name is also a deep-buttoned leather sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary constituency is an MP's seat, and a sofa of this name is a seat for sitting on.

clue.text: She comes up with a stick

indicators.note: in a down light, comes up means the phrase reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a rod is a stick or pole

explanation.surface: A woman appears carrying a walking stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' turns A ROD upwards; the result is a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so any woman so called can be referred to by the pronoun.

indicators.note: out of here means the letters of danger are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone strayed away from peril.
explanation.definitionFit: Roaming freely over an area, as cattle range over a plain.

clue.text: Shakespearean character Is found in complicated plot

indicators.note: found in tells us one piece is placed inside the other
complicated means the letters of plot are tangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A figure from the Bard turns up in an intricate storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' scrambles the fodder and 'found in' places the other piece within it; the capital on 'Is' is only surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Falstaff's swaggering companion appears in Henry IV Part 2, Henry V and The Merry Wives of Windsor.

definitions.meaning: military combat, as troops seeing combat

explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers in combat are in it, and a case brought in court is also called one.

definitions.meaning: components that let shafts rotate with low friction

explanation.definitionFit: Navigators take compass headings, and ball or roller components in engines carry rotating shafts.

clue.text: Telephone kiosks for those who want to talk all the time?

definitions.text: Telephone kiosks for those who want to talk all the time?

parts.words: Telephone kiosks for those who want to talk all the time?
parts.note: the whole is read as phone booths for people who gab, while the word means talkative people themselves

explanation.surface: Phone booths designed for compulsive talkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonstop talkers are called by this name, which split in two would be booths for gossip.

definitions.meaning: to step lightly, as in the phrase about tripping the light fantastic

explanation.definitionFit: A short outing is a jaunt of that name, and stepping nimbly in dance is also described with the word.

parts.note: read literally: of the two armies on the board, the pale-coloured one

explanation.surface: A look at the fun, less serious aspects of chess.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the pale pieces form one army, which moves first, opposed to black.

clue.text: He goes forward or back in play

definitions.text: He goes forward or back in play

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back tells us the little word or is read from its end to its start

explanation.surface: An actor moves upstage and downstage during a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: HE read forward, then OR read back, gives the leading figure of a play, who is also a character in Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal male character in a drama is its protagonist.

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep someone's property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A complete stranger.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreigner or someone not belonging is a stranger from elsewhere.

clue.text: Tour right round a south western city

indicators.note: round suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A trip goes around a West Country city.
explanation.walkthrough: The city is Cornwall's county town, in England's far south-west.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral city in Cornwall, the only city in that county.

clue.text: They restore plush, in a way

definitions.text: They restore plush, in a way

indicators.note: in a way here hints that the letters are put together differently, as in another fashion

explanation.surface: Craftspeople who refurbish velvet fabric after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' rearranges the letters of RESTORE and PLUSH together; the whole clue also describes the furniture tradespeople.
explanation.definitionFit: These tradespeople pad and recover chairs and sofas, often with plush fabric.

indicators.note: carries means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: a steamer is a steam-powered ship

explanation.surface: A vessel flies the correct flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow flag or ribbon flown from a mast.

clue.text: In which the innocent align themselves with the guilty

definitions.text: In which the innocent align themselves with the guilty

parts.words: In which the innocent align themselves with the guilty
parts.note: read literally: blameless people standing in a row beside a suspect so a witness can pick him out

explanation.surface: Decent people siding with wrongdoers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'align themselves with' sounds like taking sides, but means standing in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A police line-up where a witness picks out a suspect among volunteers.

clue.text: Put off before I made a speech and went off

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of what follows

parts.note: to put someone off doing something is to discourage them
taken as written
orated means delivered a speech

explanation.surface: Someone discouraged, gave an address and then left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went off' looks like leaving, but means going bad, as food does.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone bad has declined in quality, the same decline as worsening.

clue.text: About to take successful action to recover

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a coup is a successful stroke or triumph

explanation.surface: Someone is on the point of making a winning move.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain money that was lost or spent is to get it back.

clue.text: A point we returned to once more

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass

indicators.note: returned means the little word we is turned round to read backwards

explanation.surface: We came back to one particular place again.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something again from the start is doing it afresh.

clue.text: Interminably Isabel enthuses about a tree

indicators.note: without its ends: the run is taken from inside the words, losing the outer letters

explanation.surface: Isabel goes on and on in raptures about a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the outer letters from 'Isabel enthuses' and the tree sits at the start of what remains; 'about' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the white poplar, a European tree with silvery leaves.

indicators.note: damaged suggests the four letters of the word when are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: Something felled once it was harmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber chopped with an axe has been felled or shaped by blows.

clue.text: Desert one's post, though left in charge?

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

explanation.surface: A sentry abandons duty, even though he was put in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left in charge' reads as a deputy, but it is L inside FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To run away from danger or duty is to abscond.

indicators.note: sounding tells us the word for dull is said out loud and written another way

parts.note: slow can mean dull-witted or boring

explanation.surface: A fruit that sounds boring.
explanation.definitionFit: The small sour blackthorn berry used to flavour gin.

parts.note: read not as a dramatic defeat but as the loss of feeling and consciousness brought on by a stroke

explanation.definitionFit: The old medical term for a sudden stroke with loss of sensation and movement; also a fit of rage.

parts.note: former students of a school or college, the 'perhaps' warning that schoolchildren is one example

explanation.definitionFit: Graduates or former students of an institution are its old boys and girls.

clue.text: Wild sprees? Very strong coffee required

indicators.note: wild tells us the letters of sprees run out of control into a new order

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

explanation.surface: After riotous binges you need a powerful shot of caffeine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' scrambles the fodder; 'Very' gives a two-letter adverb and 'required' merely links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A concentrated Italian brew forced through finely ground beans.

indicators.note: ends picks out the final letter of the word holiday

parts.note: early means before the right time

explanation.surface: The yearly vacation is over before it should be.
explanation.definitionFit: Something annual happens once every twelve months.
